title: Get Equal Substrings Within Budget
summary: Given strings s and t of equal length and an integer maxCost, find the longest substring of s that can be transformed into the corresponding substring of t with a cost not exceeding maxCost, where the cost is the absolute difference between ASCII values of corresponding characters.
statement: Given strings s and t of equal length and an integer maxCost, find the longest substring of s that can be transformed into the corresponding substring of t with a cost not exceeding maxCost, where the cost is the absolute difference between ASCII values of corresponding characters.
constraints: s and t have equal positive length; max_cost is nonnegative.
reference_solution:
def longest_equal_substring_budget(s, t, max_cost):
 left=cost=best=0
 for right in range(len(s)):
  cost+=abs(ord(s[right])-ord(t[right]))
  while cost>max_cost:cost-=abs(ord(s[left])-ord(t[left]));left+=1
  best=max(best,right-left+1)
 return best
hints: Convert each aligned character pair into a nonnegative change cost.
A sliding window is valid while its cost sum is at most max_cost.
Add the right cost; repeatedly remove left costs while over budget; retain the maximum length.
Because costs are nonnegative, advancing left is the only way to restore an over-budget window.
editorial: Because costs are nonnegative, advancing left is the only way to restore an over-budget window.

tests.explanation: Costs 1,1,1,2 allow the first three positions within budget three.
Every change costs two, so the longest affordable substring has length one.
